title: Trouble whichever way one turns
odia:
ଏଣୁ ମାଇଲେ ଗୋ ହତ୍ୟା
ତେଣୁ ମାଇଲେ ବ୍ରହ୍ମ ହତ୍ୟା।
literal_meaning: Strike this way, and it is cow-killing; strike that way, and it is the killing of a Brahmin.
meaning_odia: ଏପଟେ ଗଲେ ଏକ ଅନର୍ଥ, ସେପଟେ ଗଲେ ଆଉ ଏକ ଅନର୍ଥ—କୌଣସି ପଥ ସହଜ ବା ନିରାପଦ ଲାଗୁନଥିବା ଦୋସନ୍ଧିର କଥା। କେଉଁ କାମଟି କରିବା ଉଚିତ, ତାହା ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବା କଠିନ ହୁଏ।
explanation: Either direction seems to lead to a serious wrong. The Odia Vasa gloss explains this as a dilemma in which one cannot decide what to do. The two religiously charged acts give force to the feeling that no available choice is harmless.
usage_example: Two urgent responsibilities require the same limited time; attending to either means failing the other. Someone might use the saying to express that bind. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The saying frames both cow-killing and Brahmin-killing as grave wrongs within its religious vocabulary. The balanced this way / that way construction closes off an easy escape and turns that imagery into an expression of indecision.

odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ପଥରେ ଅନର୍ଥ ଦେଖି କଣ କରିବା ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରି ନପାରିବା।
english_summary: A dilemma in which either choice seems to lead to harm.
